description.undefined: An ontology for describing changes between OWL ontology versions and the logical and computational impact of those changes

abstract.value: As any other engineering product, ontologies evolve during their lifecycle due to several reasons such as accommodating new requirements or fixing issues. To keep track of these changes, several tools have defined ad-hoc formalisms to define and manage them. However, some of them are not based on standard interoperable languages such as RDF, and the RDF-based ones cover a limited set of changes. In this paper, we present the OWL Change Ontology (OCH), an ontology to capture changes in ontologies. Developed following the LOT methodology, OCH provides a declarative framework for documenting ontology changelogs. With this approach, ontologies gain a valuable resource to improve their lifecycle management, while associated semantic products such as declarative mappings (e.g., RML) and validation shapes (e.g., SHACL) can take advantage of standardized and machine-readable changelogs to streamline their schema evolution.

bibliographicCitation.value: Conde-Herreros, D. Pernisch, R., Poveda-Villalón, M., Corcho, O., & Chaves-Fraga, D. (2024). OCH: The OWL Change Ontology

comment.en: The outcome of evaluating the impact of an ontological change, change set or changelog. An assessment is always relative to a pair of ontology versions, stated with :prevVersion and :newVersion, and where reasoning is involved to an entailment regime and a reasoner. Impact is reified rather than asserted as a type of the change itself, because whether a change is effectual holds only relative to those parameters.

comment.en: The change alters the set of entailments. An added axiom is effectual when it is not entailed by the previous version; a removed axiom is effectual when it is not entailed by the new version.

The change does not alter the set of entailments. An added axiom is ineffectual when it is already entailed by the previous version; a removed axiom is ineffectual when it remains entailed by the new version.

The logical impact could not be decided, for instance because the entailment check exceeded the time limit stated in :reasoningTimeout, because the reasoner is incomplete for the expressivity of the ontology, or because one of the versions could not be loaded. The value is asserted positively so that an undecided change remains distinguishable from an unassessed one.
The top term that encompasses the possible effects of a change on the set of axioms entailed by an ontology.

comment.en: A minimal subset of an ontology that entails a given axiom. Entailment justifications explain why an ineffectual change is ineffectual, and are the basis on which ineffectual changes are further categorised. A single change may have several justifications. Not to be confused with :justification, which records the rationale behind a change in natural language.
